findings.title: Unconditional URL SSRF validation crashes startup with an uncaught ValidationError on an existing config
findings.problem: The new field_validator raises ValueError for any URL that is non-http(s), malformed, metadata, or link-local, so Settings() raises pydantic.ValidationError at load time. triggarr/config.py:ensure_config() catches only tomllib.TOMLDecodeError/UnicodeDecodeError around load_settings(); its docstring explicitly states 'pydantic.ValidationError (schema bug) continue to propagate uncaught' — that assumption held while URL content was never validated at load, and this change breaks it by routing user-supplied config data into the same path. Reproduced: a config containing radarr.Default.url = "radarr:7878" (no scheme — a plausible hand-edited value, and a value the pre-change code accepted) now makes ensure_config raise ValidationError instead of the friendly _log_corrupt_config_and_exit path, so the daemon dies with a bare traceback out of asyncio.run(_run()) and the operator gets no config path, no .toml.bak restore hint, and no way to fix it via the web UI (the app never starts). Existing tests all pass because no fixture uses a URL the validator rejects.

findings.why_it_matters: A previously-working install can fail to boot after upgrade with an unreadable traceback and no in-app recovery route, since the settings UI is unreachable when startup aborts.

findings.title: Loopback URL accepted at config load but rejected by the settings form, wedging save_settings
findings.problem: The model validator uses the relaxed validate_arr_url_config (loopback permitted — the stated D-01/D-02 intent), but triggarr/web/routes.py:561 in save_settings still calls the strict validate_arr_url, which returns (False, 'Blocked address') for loopback literals. Verified directly: 'http://127.0.0.1:7878' and 'http://[::1]:7878' are config:True / form:False. The settings template renders inst.url back into the form field (templates/settings.html:173), so a user whose triggarr.toml legitimately holds a loopback *arr URL — exactly the same-host homelab case this change was made to permit — cannot save ANY settings change: every POST resubmits that URL, hits the strict check, and returns a bare 303 redirect back to the settings page with no error shown to the user (only a server-side logger.warning). The relaxation is half-applied: config load was loosened, the form path was not.

findings.title: Config-load SSRF rejection is unrecoverable via UI — bad URL in triggarr.toml hard-crashes startup with a raw ValidationError traceback
findings.problem: The new validator makes InstanceConfig construction fail for metadata/link-local/non-http/malformed URLs. That rejection is intended (D-01/D-02) and correctly implemented, but the FAILURE PRESENTATION is not covered by the plan. I read the full startup chain: startup.py:192 calls ensure_config(), and config.py:333-373 catches ONLY tomllib.TOMLDecodeError and UnicodeDecodeError, translating those into a friendly loguru.error + sys.exit(1). config.py:345 explicitly documents that `pydantic.ValidationError` (schema bug) continues to propagate uncaught. Before this diff that carve-out was reasonable — a ValidationError from triggarr.toml was near-unreachable, since no field validator could reject a plausible hand-edited value. This diff makes ValidationError reachable from ordinary user data (a URL typed into triggarr.toml). Consequence: Triggarr exits with an uncaught pydantic traceback out of asyncio.run(_run()), not the friendly 'edit your config and restart' line the corrupt-TOML path gets. Worse for recovery: the web UI (the documented place to fix instance URLs, per config.py DEFAULT_CONFIG 'Instance configuration is managed through the web UI') never starts, because ensure_config runs before the app does. The user must hand-edit /config/triggarr.toml inside the container to recover — with only a traceback to tell them which instance is at fault. This is a container that crash-loops with no actionable operator message. Note this is the exact class of UX gap TEST-02 already fixed for corrupt TOML; the same treatment was simply never extended to ValidationError because it was previously unreachable.

findings.why_it_matters: Docker-first deployment (ghcr.io/thejuran/triggarr). A crash-looping container whose only diagnostic is a pydantic traceback, and whose documented repair surface (the web UI) cannot start, turns an intended security hardening into an operator-visible outage with no in-product recovery path.
